git.name: Git
git.why: Keeps a history of every change so you can always go back.

windows: Choose “Install for me”, or download Git for Windows from the page we open.
Run the installer and keep the suggested options.
Come back here and choose “Check again”.
macos: Follow the pop-up to install the developer tools.
Come back here and choose “Check again”.
linux: Install Git with your package manager, for example: sudo apt install git
Come back here and choose “Check again”.

flutter.name: Flutter SDK
flutter.why: The toolkit that turns your app into real iOS and Android apps.

windows: Open the install guide and pick Windows, then Android.
Download the Flutter SDK zip and unzip it somewhere simple, like C:\src\flutter (no spaces).
Add the folder flutter\bin to your PATH (the guide shows how).
macos: Open the install guide and pick macOS.
Download the Flutter SDK and unzip it in your home folder.
Add flutter/bin to your PATH (the guide shows how).
linux: Open the install guide and pick Linux.
Download the Flutter SDK and extract it in your home folder.
Add flutter/bin to your PATH (the guide shows how).

android.name: Android toolchain
android.why: Lets Studio build and test Android apps. Needed before you can publish to Google Play.

issues.no_sdk: Android Studio (which includes the Android SDK) isn’t installed yet.
issues.licenses: The Android licenses still need to be accepted. This is a one-time step.
issues.cmdline_tools: One Android component (command-line tools) is missing.
issues.needs_flutter: Install the Flutter SDK first. Then we can check Android.
issues.other: Flutter found a problem with the Android setup. Open the details to see what.

no_sdk: Download Android Studio from the page we open and install it with the default options.
Start Android Studio once and let it finish downloading the Android SDK.
Come back here and choose “Check again”.
licenses: Choose “Accept licenses” and answer y to each question in the terminal.
cmdline_tools: Open Android Studio, then Settings, then Android SDK, then the SDK Tools tab.
Tick “Android SDK Command-line Tools”, press Apply and wait for it to finish.
Come back here and choose “Check again”.
other: Open the technical details below and look at the lines marked with ✗ or !.
Fix them (Android Studio’s SDK Manager fixes most), then choose “Check again”.
needs_flutter: Finish the Flutter SDK step above first.

claude.name: Claude Code
claude.why: The AI that writes your app. It runs on your own Claude account.

windows: Choose “Install for me”, or follow the install guide on the page we open.
Restart Studio so it can find Claude.
macos: Open the install guide and follow the macOS steps.
Restart Studio so it can find Claude.
linux: Open the install guide and follow the Linux steps.
Restart Studio so it can find Claude.

updateSteps: In a terminal, run: claude update

claudeLogin.name: Claude account
claudeLogin.why: You sign in yourself through the official Claude Code. Studio only checks whether you are signed in.

unknown.title: Something unexpected happened
unknown.fix: Try again. If it keeps happening, restart Studio and check the log file in Settings.

db.title: Studio couldn’t read its own data
db.fix: Restart Studio. If this keeps happening, your projects are still safe in their folders; check the log file in Settings.

io.title: Studio couldn’t access a file or folder
io.fix: Check that the folder exists and isn’t read-only or open in another program, then try again.

not_found.title: We couldn’t find that
not_found.fix: It may have been removed. Go back to your projects and try again.

invalid.title: That doesn’t look right
invalid.fix: Check what you entered and try again.

tool_missing.title: {{tool}} isn’t available yet
tool_missing.fix: Open setup to install it. Studio walks you through it.

command_failed.title: A tool reported a problem
command_failed.fix: Open setup to check your tools, then try again. The technical details are in the log file (Settings).

timeout.title: This is taking too long
timeout.fix: Check your internet connection and try again.

path_exists.title: That folder already exists
path_exists.fix: Pick another name or another projects folder in Settings.

unsafe.title: Studio stopped to protect your files
unsafe.fix: That folder isn’t a Studio project inside your projects folder. Nothing was deleted.

pty.title: The terminal couldn’t start
pty.fix: Close the terminal and try again. If it still fails, restart Studio.
